_comment: The one op in op_defs/basic_ops/xccl_ops.py that had no workload file anywhere
in the repo, on any backend, and the only one that measures a *real* point-to-
point transfer: vendor_impl_run does dist.isend on rank src_device and
dist.irecv on rank dst_device, so bus_size is the bytes that actually cross one
link, one way.
This is the gap left by device2device.json, which despite its name copies within
a single device (Device2DeviceOp allocates src and dst on the same one), so its
648 GB/s is local HBM and no hop is in it. Until this file existed, NVLink-vs-
NeuronLink point-to-point was uncovered on both backends -- the collectives
measure a whole ring, not a link.
world_size is 2 because a send/recv pair is two ranks whatever the group is.
Which *chips* those two ranks sit on is chosen by the launcher's --device list,
the same way the d2d_hop0/hop1/hop2 labels do it, so the hop-count comparison
is three launches of this one file:
--device 0,1  same chip, no NeuronLink hop
--device 0,4  chip 0 -> chip 1, one hop
--device 0,8  chip 0 -> chip 2, two hops (on the 4x4 torus chip 0's
neighbours are 1, 3, 4 and 12, so 2 is not one of them)
On a GPU box it is --device 0,1 against a pair on different NVSwitch domains.
int8 is in the dtype list on purpose. int8 all_gather and all_to_all are ~200x
off bf16 on the Neuron stack while the same bytes in bf16 are fine, and the probe
narrowed that to a serialized issue path rather than a host fallback. A p2p case
is the simplest possible collective -- one send, one recv, no algorithm choice --
so if int8 is slow here too the problem is below the collective algorithm, and if
it is not, it is in the algorithm.
The second case is the configuration README.md in this directory already
documents for this op -- [1024, 2097152] int8, 2 GiB one way -- which had no file
to live in. That README also describes p2p as a pairwise sweep over every pair of
devices; the op def does not do that (src_device and dst_device are single ranks),
so an all-pairs matrix is one launch per pair, as the three --device lists above.
